features.name: GitHub Actions
features.description: GitHub's pipeline equivalent to Azure DevOps pipelines for validating code during pull requests and automating workflows.

features.name: GitHub Issues
features.description: GitHub's work item equivalent to Azure DevOps work items for defining and tracking features and user stories.

features.name: GitHub Copilot
features.description: AI-assisted development feature mentioned as a reason to consider moving to GitHub, though not the primary focus of the decision.
caveats: Not the main reason for migration decision

features.name: GitHub Projects
features.description: Collections of issues from different repositories in GitHub, different from Azure DevOps projects which serve as containers for all resources.
caveats: Not a container for all resources like in DevOps

features.name: GitHub Environments
features.description: Environment management in GitHub repositories with configurable properties and attributes for deployment gates and controlled delivery.

features.name: GitHub repository permissions per repository
features.description: Permissions are managed at the repository level in GitHub, with teams used to group repositories and assign access to users.

features.name: GitHub Team license
features.description: GitHub Team license available at 4 USD per user per month without single sign-on support, requiring personal developer accounts.
caveats: No single sign-on support
Requires personal developer accounts
Difficult to manage for teams larger than 5 developers

features.name: GitHub Enterprise license
features.description: GitHub Enterprise license at 21 USD allowing Entra integration, single sign-on, data residency options, SOC reports, environment protection rules, and more action minutes.
caveats: Includes Azure DevOps basic license automatically
Available through Visual Studio subscriptions but via Enterprise agreement only

features.name: GitHub Enterprise Copilot access
features.description: GitHub Enterprise license now includes Copilot access for all users with pay-as-you-go usage charging, no credits included.
caveats: No credits included
Pay-as-you-go pricing model
Changed a few months ago

features.name: Data residency for GitHub Enterprise Cloud
features.description: GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports data residency in multiple regions including US, EU, Japan, and Australia, with Brazil, India and more regions planned.
caveats: Requires ghe.com subdomain instead of github.com
Some tools may not support the new URL format
No public repositories allowed
Requires enterprise managed users

features.name: Enterprise managed users requirement
features.description: When using data residency, enterprise managed users is mandatory and personal accounts cannot be used, eliminating anonymous access.
caveats: No public repositories allowed
No anonymous access

features.name: In-region AI processing
features.description: In-region AI processing available for Europe and US regions with 10% higher AI credit cost.
caveats: Costs 10% more in AI credits
Limited to Europe and US regions
Data residency feature
No marketplace support

features.name: GitHub Issues sub-issues and dependencies
features.description: GitHub Issues now supports sub-issues, issue types, and dependencies, though still lighter than Azure DevOps work items.
caveats: Less customizable than DevOps work items
New features added this year
Still lighter than Azure DevOps work items

features.name: Copilot MCP server for DevOps
features.description: Copilot integration with Azure DevOps including MCP server support for code review, app agents, and work delegation to cloud agents.
caveats: Only through integration
Some features work better with GitHub repositories
MCP server already available

features.name: GitHub and DevOps cooperation
features.description: Repositories can be migrated to GitHub while maintaining DevOps project management, work items, dashboards, wikis, and pipelines, with choice to run pipelines on DevOps or GitHub workflows.
caveats: Requires repositories to be on GitHub
Must choose between DevOps pipelines or GitHub workflows or combine both

features.name: GitHub Actions triggers
features.description: GitHub Actions provide more trigger options compared to Azure DevOps pipelines. You can trigger actions when new issues are created or other events, whereas DevOps pipelines can only run when repository changes occur or pull requests are created.
caveats: DevOps requires service hooks for custom triggers

features.name: Azure Boards app integration
features.description: The Azure Boards app connects GitHub repositories to Azure DevOps projects, enabling linking of commits to work items, pull requests to work items, and status badge synchronization between platforms.
caveats: One repository maps to one DevOps project
Linking happens automatically via commit hash or pull request mentions

features.name: Copilot cloud agent for pull requests
features.description: DevOps users can hand work items to a Copilot cloud agent which creates draft pull requests automatically. This functionality is now available in GA on DevOps, providing the same capability as GitHub's agent feature.
features.status_evidence_quote: Same functionality is now available already in in GA on on DevOps
caveats: Creates drafts that need review
Available in both GitHub and DevOps

features.name: Code review and Copilot app for Azure repositories
features.description: New agentic app released this month supporting code review and Copilot functionality for Azure repositories, extending GitHub's development experience to DevOps repositories.
caveats: GitHub remains the primary platform for agentic development

features.name: Public project retirement on DevOps
features.description: Microsoft is ending support for public projects on Azure DevOps next year, affecting Business Central symbol feeds that depend on public artifact feeds for public access.
caveats: GitHub package service appears public but requires tokens
Requires alternative solution for symbol feeds

features.name: GitHub Enterprise Importer tool
features.description: Migration tool for moving repositories from Azure DevOps to GitHub, migrating pull requests, user history, work items, links, attachments, and branch policies. Supports data residency options.
caveats: User scope and cross policies not migrated
2GB limit per commit
255 byte limit on branch names and tags
100MB per file on GitHub (400MB when migrating)
40GB per repository limit
Loses data when using basic git clone method
Need to map mannequin users to GitHub users post-migration

features.name: Branch policy migration
features.description: Migration capability that moves repository policies from Azure DevOps to GitHub during migration, excluding user scope and cross policies but including repository-level policies.
caveats: User scope policies excluded
Cross policies excluded

features.name: Azure DevOps Enterprise Live Migration tool
features.description: New migration tool supporting ghe.com migration to GitHub with data residency. Requires on-premises Linux agent. Performs validation, initial synchronization of repositories and pull requests, then incremental sync with cutover capability.
features.status_evidence_quote: It's a new tool. It's in public preview, but it have some limitations
caveats: Only supports ghe.com migration
Requires on-premises Linux machine to host agent
Limited to 30 repositories per migration
No sync back after cutover
21-day window for decision before final cutover
New since August 26
Some customers with 1000+ repositories cannot use it effectively

features.name: GH Actions Importer
features.description: Tool to migrate pipelines and actions from Azure DevOps to GitHub workflows. Can migrate Azure DevOps pipelines to GitHub Actions.
caveats: Not easy to set up
Low activity on project (last commit 25)
Depends on which actions used in Azure DevOps pipelines
Requires replacement of ALOps until ALOps has GitHub version
May need manual work for custom actions

features.name: DevOps pull request pipeline gating
features.description: Capability to connect GitHub pull requests to Azure DevOps pipelines as gates. When pull request is triggered, it runs the pipeline in DevOps and prevents PR closure if pipeline fails.
caveats: Requires setup configuration
Can be used as alternative to GitHub Actions

features.name: GitHub connection in Azure DevOps
features.description: Connection configuration in Azure Boards that links GitHub repositories to DevOps projects. Allows linking work items to GitHub pull requests and repositories.
caveats: Connection can link all repositories from project or selected ones
Part of Boards section

features.name: Live migration tool
features.description: A tool that allows migration of repositories from Azure DevOps to GitHub, supporting up to 70 repositories with automatic connection creation.
caveats: Requires Linux agent for execution
Requires personal access tokens and agent pool configuration

features.name: Copilot code review
features.description: Available in both Azure DevOps and GitHub for automated code review capabilities.

features.name: Copilot app agents in Azure repositories
features.description: Support for Copilot app agents is available in Azure DevOps repositories.

features.name: Azure DevOps remote MCP server
features.description: MCP server support available for Azure DevOps repositories.

features.name: Copilot auto fix
features.description: An agent that automatically drafts pull requests with fixes for security issues found by advanced security alerts when using advanced security features.
caveats: Requires advanced security features to be enabled

features.name: Azure DevOps plugin in Copilot Cowork
features.description: Copilot Cowork now has a plugin for Azure DevOps allowing it to work with work items for creating bugs or user stories.

features.name: Hybrid Azure Boards with GitHub connection
features.description: Ability to connect GitHub repositories to Azure DevOps Boards for hybrid work item tracking.

features.name: Copilot cloud agent
features.description: Full-featured Copilot cloud agent available only on GitHub, not on Azure DevOps repositories.
caveats: Only available on GitHub, not on Azure DevOps

features.name: Copilot cloud and Codex agents on GitHub
features.description: GitHub exclusive feature providing cloud and Codex agents for Copilot, not available on Azure DevOps.
caveats: Not available on Azure DevOps

features.name: Copilot approvals and max review
features.description: GitHub feature for Copilot-powered approvals and max settings review functionality.
caveats: GitHub exclusive feature

features.name: GitHub Actions and Pages
features.description: GitHub exclusive features including Actions for CI-CD workflows and Pages for static site hosting, not available on Azure DevOps.
caveats: Not available on Azure DevOps

features.name: AL-Go for GitHub
features.description: A DevOps solution for Business Central AL development based on a monorepo approach available for GitHub.
caveats: Based on monorepo working model
Requires agenting implementation
Still evolving and changing

features.name: GitHub workflows
features.description: YAML-based workflow automation in GitHub supporting templating and custom triggers for CI-CD, with more trigger options than Azure DevOps pipelines.
caveats: Developers need to learn GitHub interface
PowerShell tools work on both platforms

features.name: Copilot code analysis for bug detection
features.description: Consultants can ask an agent or copilot to analyze code and repositories to find bugs or identify if problems exist in the code.

quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the core business challenge this presentation addresses - organizations must decide whether to migrate from Azure DevOps to GitHub.

quotes.text: GitHub Copilot and GitHub at all is too good to ignore
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies the pull toward GitHub as a destination despite DevOps strengths - GitHub has capabilities that are hard to dismiss.

quotes.text: the main container is the project on DevOps and we need to to remember that
quotes.why_it_matters: Key structural difference - DevOps organizes work around projects while GitHub does not, affecting migration planning.

quotes.text: because project is totally different thing in in github
quotes.why_it_matters: Fundamental architectural difference between platforms that impacts how work is organized and permissions are managed.

quotes.text: if you push some change for one app, it will trigger the the pipeline or action for whole repository
quotes.why_it_matters: Monorepo limitation - requires additional filtering configuration to prevent unnecessary builds for multiple apps in one repository.

quotes.text: GitHub ALGO, it's mostly using the monorepo as a, for example, for for customer project
quotes.why_it_matters: AL-GO tooling assumes monorepo structure which differs from traditional Azure DevOps multirepo approaches used by many teams.

quotes.text: Licensing, of course, before we decide what we will do, we should understand the licensing.
quotes.why_it_matters: Licensing decisions are foundational to choosing between GitHub and DevOps solutions.

quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the cost and limitations of the basic GitHub team option.

quotes.text: the GitHub Enterprise license is already including Azure DevOps basic license.
quotes.why_it_matters: GitHub Enterprise provides dual licensing benefit, eliminating additional DevOps license costs.

quotes.text: New in this year is that the GitHub Enterprise license is including the Copilot access license.
quotes.why_it_matters: Marks a significant change in GitHub Enterprise value proposition with Copilot now included.

quotes.text: If you migrate the repositories to GitHub you can still use the project and work items and dashboards and wikis on DevOps.
